Q1: When the 5-minute idle check fires with no timer running, how should the reminder be shown to the user? (FR-010)
Why it matters: This determines notification permissions, testing approach, and whether the reminder can offer a one-click "start timer" action.
Options: A) macOS system notification banner (dismissible, non-blocking) B) Modal alert dialog that must be dismissed C) System notification with an inline "Start pomodoro" action button
Recommended: A — system notifications are the standard non-intrusive macOS pattern, require no window focus, and degrade gracefully when notifications are disabled (which the spec already accepts for v1).

Q2: How frequently should the menu bar countdown text update while a pomodoro is running? (FR-005, SC-003)
Why it matters: The cadence sets the battery/CPU budget and defines what "updates continuously" means for acceptance tests.
Options: A) Every second (MM:SS ticks visibly) B) Every 30 seconds (shows whole minutes) C) Every 60 seconds
Recommended: A — one-second updates are the familiar convention for menu bar timers and make SC-003 ("no visible divergence") directly testable.

Q3: When a user starts a pomodoro from the menu bar dropdown, how is the activity being recorded chosen? (FR-006, FR-008)
Why it matters: This defines what the activity name next to the countdown will be and whether extra UI (a picker) is needed.
Options: A) Automatically uses the app's currently selected/default activity, no choice offered B) Dropdown shows a submenu of recent activities the user picks from before starting C) Menu bar can only start a timer if an activity is already selected; otherwise it prompts the user to open the app
Recommended: B — a recent-activities submenu keeps the flow fully menu-bar-driven (SC-002) while still letting the user control what is being recorded.

Q4: If the underlying timer supports pause, should a paused (not stopped) pomodoro count as "running" for the 5-minute reminder check? (FR-008, FR-010, FR-013)
Why it matters: It decides whether reminders fire during pauses and how pause interacts with the existing finalize-on-stop session lifecycle.
Options: A) Yes — a paused timer still counts as active, so no reminders fire until it is stopped or finished B) No — a paused timer counts as idle and reminders resume after 5 idle minutes C) The timer does not support pause at all; only stop (which finalizes the session)
Recommended: A — treating a paused session as still active matches user intent (they haven't abandoned tracking) and avoids nagging users mid-session.

Q5: Should v1 provide any way for the user to turn off or snooze the 5-minute idle reminders? (FR-010)
Why it matters: This affects scope (a settings surface may be needed) and prevents the reminder from becoming noise for users who don't want it.
Options: A) No — reminders always fire every 5 idle minutes, no setting in v1 B) Yes — a simple on/off setting for idle reminders C) Yes — a "snooze" choice on each reminder that delays the next one (e.g., 15 minutes)
Recommended: A — keeps v1 scope minimal and matches the stated requirement; a setting can be added later if reminders prove noisy.
